paragraphs: Friend, here is what I see in this whole chapter. Moses keeps saying, "You must not ignore it" (Deuteronomy 22:3). A lost animal, a fallen donkey, a roof with no railing. God wants His people to look at what is right in front of them and do something about it. I spent years forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, so I know how good it feels when somebody doesn't walk past.

Then the chapter gets heavy, and I think it matters to say so. Moses lays out hard cases about marriage. In some of them the wronged person is shielded: a wife is protected from a false accusation and her husband must never divorce her (Deuteronomy 22:18-19), and a young woman who cried out in a field is told, "Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death." (Deuteronomy 22:26). Other cases are hard to read, like the man who seizes a virgin and must pay her father fifty shekels and marry her (Deuteronomy 22:28-29), and I think that one stings. Moses says, "So you must purge the evil from among you." (Deuteronomy 22:21), so sin and its harm are no small thing.

So here's your takeaway, baker. Loving your neighbor is the same whether it's a stray ox or a person's good name. Notice who needs help, step in, and protect people who can't protect themselves. And remember that Moses is still going, because his speech isn't over yet.
